judged_text: destroy calls host.destroy on the result of where(...).first without a nil check, so a missing id raises NoMethodError on nil. DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id for an already-deleted or bogus id returns a 500 instead of success_json or a 4xx; concurrent deletes from two admin tabs hit this.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` followed by `host.destroy` with no nil check. If the record doesn't exist (bogus id or already deleted), `host` will be nil and calling `destroy` will raise a `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 instead of a controlled success/4xx response.
